title: Jimmy 'Cry Cry' Hawkins and McBee's first gig in Wichita
summary: Hawkins recruited him from the school band and he played his first gig in Wichita.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Aluminum bass. And so I tried to play something and, tried to play some boogie woogie on it like I had heard on the juke box. And so a couple of days later I got some buddies to join me and we would try to play some boogie woogie or something you know. There was a trombone player, saxophone player, and there was a drummer. No piano player. So we had a good time. And then a couple of months later we were in the same room. Somebody knocks on the door. And Wesley, my buddy, alto player, who was a star forward for the basketball team, he opened the door and there was this guy in all of this color, you know, and he was about the size of Miles Davis. Right? And his hair slicked back, and a gold tooth here. And he says, “Hey man,” he says, “I’m looking for Cecil McBee. Which one of you is Cecil McBee?” Because we were sitting down resting. And I raised my hand. And my buddy told me, “Hey man, that’s Jimmy ‘Cry Cry’ Hawkins, man.” I said, “Jimmy ‘Cry Cry’.” And Jimmy “Cry Cry” said, “Cecil McBee here?” I said, “Yeah I’m Cecil McBee.” He says, “Hey man I hear you play the bass pretty good man. You play it pretty good.” He say, “I got a band. You gonna play with my band?” And my buddy said, “Oh my, oh man, he knows Cecil McBee?” And so I ended up going with Jimmy “Cry Cry” to Wichita, Kansas on my first gig, sitting in the rear of this car in

early October. The window was out. There was a towel to prevent the wind from coming in. I played my first gig with Jimmy “Cry Cry,” with — standing on his head. This was before James Brown. He would stand on his head literally crying while he would hold the mic — he would support his body with his right hand and hold the mic literally upside down, crying ‘cause his baby left him. Right? That was my first gig.
And seriously, to this day, Jimmy “Cry Cry” is a great part of Tulsa’s history.
